spans.text: To directly compare neural activity during craving/urge states in women and men with CD and PG, and control participants (CPs) without either disorder, we recruited 114 participants for functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI).
Data from this large independent sample have not been previously published.
Functional images were acquired in the axial plane parallel to the AC-PC line (TR/TE=1500/27 ms, flip angle=60°, field of view=220 × 220 mm, and 25 × 5 mm slices).

value: A diagnostic group × video type interaction was observed in perigenual ACC/medial PFC, where CD participants showed greater activity for the cocaine videos compared with sad and gambling videos, while control participants exhibited significantly lower activity to cocaine videos compared with gambling and sad videos.
This region has been previously associated with cocaine craving in cocaine dependence, replicating and extending prior findings in predominantly or solely male samples.

value: A diagnostic group × video type interaction was seen in a region of dorsomedial PFC/dorsal ACC. Activity was selectively increased in a video-specific and diagnosis-specific fashion: gambling videos in PG participants, cocaine videos in CD participants, and sad videos in control participants.
The matched responding in this region suggests that activity underlies the motivational/emotional response generated for these videos.
